description: Structured eval definitions for the X-Ray Tracing Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across platforms (EC2 systemd, ECS Fargate sidecar, EKS DaemonSet, Lambda Powertools), SDK languages (Java, Python, Node.js), sampling rules (default vs custom), observability (CloudWatch ServiceLens, X-Ray groups), OpenTelemetry / ADOT migration, and prerequisite failure branches (missing IAM GetSamplingRules permission, oversampled Default rule at 100% on high-traffic service). Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: Java Spring Boot on EC2 with systemd daemon and default sampling
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — EC2 systemd, Java SDK v2, default sampling, annotations
eval_cases.prompt: Enable X-Ray distributed tracing on a Java Spring Boot application named "orders-api" running on EC2 instances in us-east-1. The app uses AWS SDK v2 (DynamoDB, S3, SQS). Instance profile role ec2-orders-role. Deploy the X-Ray daemon 4.x via systemd. Use the aws-xray-recorder-sdk-core and aws-xray-recorder-sdk-aws-sdk-v2 Maven packages. Default sampling rule (reservoir 1/s, rate 5%). Annotations: order_id, environment=production, region=us-east-1. Metadata: request_body_size. Enable CloudWatch ServiceLens. Account: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
SERVICE: orders-api
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓]      Platform — EC2, systemd daemon
  [✓]      Daemon — aws-xray-daemon:4.x via systemd (UDP 2000)
  [✓]      SDK instrumentation — Java, aws-xray-recorder-sdk-core + aws-sdk-v2, XRayServletFilter
  [✓]      AWS SDK patched — TracingHandler on DynamoDB, S3, SQS clients
  [✓]      Sampling rule — Default (reservoir 1/s, rate 5%)
  [✓]      IAM role — ec2-orders-role has xray:PutTraceSegments + PutTelemetryRecords + GetSamplingRules + GetSamplingTargets
  [✓]      Annotations — order_id, environment=production, region=us-east-1
  [✓]      Metadata — request_body_size
  [✓]      Service map — generated from traces
  [✓]      CloudWatch ServiceLens — integrated
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws xray get-sampling-rules
  aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name ec2-orders-role
  aws xray get-service-graph --start-time 2026-08-10T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-08-10T23:59:59Z

eval_cases.name: ECS Fargate Python Flask with ADOT Collector and custom sampling
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — ADOT Collector sidecar, OTel SDK, custom sampling on checkout
eval_cases.prompt: Enable distributed tracing on a Python Flask service named "payments-api-prod" running on ECS Fargate (cluster payments-prod) in us-east-1. Use the ADOT Collector (OpenTelemetry) as a sidecar container instead of the X-Ray daemon. Python 3.11 with opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask and opentelemetry-instrumentation-botocore. Task role payments-task with X-Ray write permissions. Custom sampling rule payments-checkout (100% on POST /checkout, reservoir 10/s). Default rule at 5% for all other endpoints. Annotations: customer_id, environment=production. Metadata: response_status. Enable CloudWatch ServiceLens. Account: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
SERVICE: payments-api-prod
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓]      Platform — ECS Fargate, cluster payments-prod
  [✓]      Daemon — ADOT Collector (aws-otel-collector) sidecar, gRPC 4317
  [✓]      SDK instrumentation — Python 3.11, opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask + opentelemetry-instrumentation-botocore
  [✓]      AWS SDK patched — BotocoreInstrumentor for DynamoDB, S3, SQS
  [✓]      Sampling rule — Default (reservoir 1/s, rate 5%), custom payments-checkout (reservoir 10/s, rate 100% on POST /checkout)
  [✓]      IAM role — payments-task has xray:PutTraceSegments + PutTelemetryRecords + GetSamplingRules + GetSamplingTargets
  [✓]      Annotations — customer_id, environment=production
  [✓]      Metadata — response_status
  [✓]      Service map — generated from traces
  [✓]      CloudWatch ServiceLens — integrated
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws xray get-sampling-rules
  aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition payments-api-prod
  aws xray get-service-graph --start-time 2026-08-10T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-08-10T23:59:59Z

eval_cases.name: Node.js Express on ECS Fargate without GetSamplingRules permission
eval_cases.prompt: Enable X-Ray tracing on a Node.js Express service named "search-api-prod" on ECS Fargate in us-east-1. Use the X-Ray SDK (aws-xray-sdk-core) with the xray-daemon:4.1 sidecar. The task role search-task currently has xray:PutTraceSegments and xray:PutTelemetryRecords but does NOT have xray:GetSamplingRules or xray:GetSamplingTargets. The operator has not added these permissions. Default sampling rule at 5%. Account: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
SERVICE: search-api-prod
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✓]      Platform — ECS Fargate
  [✓]      Daemon — aws-xray-daemon:4.1 sidecar (UDP 2000)
  [✓]      SDK instrumentation — Node.js, aws-xray-sdk-core, Express middleware
  [✗]      IAM role — search-task is MISSING xray:GetSamplingRules and xray:GetSamplingTargets. Without these, the SDK cannot fetch central sampling rules and falls back to local default (1/s, fixed). The rules you configure in the X-Ray console are NEVER applied. Attach the AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess managed policy or add both actions to the inline policy.
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name search-task
  aws iam list-role-policies --role-name search-task
  aws iam get-role-policy --role-name search-task --policy-name <policy>

eval_cases.name: Lambda Python with Powertools tracing and custom sampling rule
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — Powertools decorators, custom high-value sampling, annotations
eval_cases.prompt: Enable X-Ray tracing on a Lambda function named "checkout-handler-prod" in us-east-1. Runtime Python 3.11. Use AWS Lambda Powertools for tracing (capture_lambda_handler and capture_method decorators). The function calls DynamoDB and SQS via boto3. Lambda execution role checkout-exec-role (needs X-Ray write permissions). Custom sampling rule checkout-high-value (100% sampling, reservoir 5/s) matching the Lambda service name. Annotations: order_id, customer_id, environment=production. Metadata: processing_time_ms. Enable CloudWatch ServiceLens. Account: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
SERVICE: checkout-handler-prod
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓]      Platform — Lambda, Python 3.11, built-in daemon (no sidecar)
  [✓]      Daemon — Lambda built-in (TracingConfig Mode=Active)
  [✓]      SDK instrumentation — AWS Lambda Powertools v2, @tracer.capture_lambda_handler + @tracer.capture_method
  [✓]      AWS SDK patched — Powertools auto-patches boto3
  [✓]      Sampling rule — Default (reservoir 1/s, rate 5%), custom checkout-high-value (reservoir 5/s, rate 100%)
  [✓]      IAM role — checkout-exec-role has xray:PutTraceSegments + PutTelemetryRecords + GetSamplingRules + GetSamplingTargets
  [✓]      Annotations — order_id, customer_id, environment=production
  [✓]      Metadata — processing_time_ms
  [✓]      Service map — generated from traces (Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS)
  [✓]      CloudWatch ServiceLens — integrated
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name checkout-handler-prod --query 'TracingConfig'
  aws xray get-sampling-rules
  aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name checkout-exec-role

eval_cases.name: EKS high-traffic API with Default sampling rule set to 100%
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — Default rule at 100% generates massive trace volume and cost
eval_cases.prompt: Enable X-Ray tracing on a high-traffic Node.js API named "media-api-prod" on EKS in us-east-1. The service handles 5000 requests/second. The operator wants the Default sampling rule set to FixedRate=1.0 (100%) so that "every request is traced." Use the aws-xray-sdk-core with the X-Ray daemon DaemonSet. Node.js 20 with Express. Pod IRSA role media-api-xray-role. Annotations: user_id, content_type. The EKS cluster is media-prod. Account: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
SERVICE: media-api-prod
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✓]      Platform — EKS, cluster media-prod
  [✓]      Daemon — aws-xray-daemon DaemonSet (UDP 2000)
  [✓]      SDK instrumentation — Node.js 20, aws-xray-sdk-core, Express middleware
  [✗]      Sampling rule — Default rule at FixedRate=1.0 (100%) for a 5000 req/s service would generate ~432M traces/day. At $5 per 1M traces, this is ~$2,160/day in X-Ray ingestion costs. Keep the Default rule at 5% and create custom rules scoped to critical endpoints. NEVER set FixedRate=1.0 on the Default rule for high-traffic services.
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws xray get-sampling-rules --query 'SamplingRuleRecords[?SamplingRule.RuleName==`Default`].SamplingRule.FixedRate'
  aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/XRay --metric-name TotalTraceCount --statistics Sum --period 3600 --start-time 2026-08-09T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-08-10T00:00:00Z
